scope: Finite ordinary closure-template source/AST review only. The current scientific run, receipts/results, arrays/media and code execution were not read or run.

verified_static_contracts: The template requires actual terminal identity/tool exit arguments and a final pass/not_pass launch with exactly one invocation; it refuses a running launch. It checks current HEAD against the frozen protocol source baseline and preserves science version0.5.0/science baselineb1334bb6a83ba9a0efab7bdba7bd39722146f024.

PASS is computed from tool exit0, both actual helper/outer pass, verified cleanup/no stop, complete helper seal, batch success, display pass and the complete shared-display seal. Any false/missing required execution condition gives NOT_PASS. It does not rewrite original helper/result/response flags or promote a producer-only result to independent qualification.

Result/response/batch statuses, cached gates, original call counts and diagnostic row counts are copied from final ordinary JSON. Missing result counts are None; missing diagnostics remain None; real0 counts are retained only when their ordinary result data exists. No zero force, gap, residual or not_run is synthesized from unavailable files.

A viewer last-observation row is used only when accepted index/original target/leg/d/stateSHA all match the actual last saved state. Absent observation does not cause new geometry evaluation or replacement by q_out/global J. Null no-hit remains null, and positive finite ray is not described as proof of effective clamp/contact.

The physical table and notes retain half-model actuator R, weighted q_out, signed lower-body total/material/Hu ON-body force with opposite holding reaction. Finite rays, unsigned tip distances, node-window diagnostics, continuous pressure and effective grip are distinguished. Short.5 loading is not1.2 full cycle, unloading/release, full-column HP, stability/ranking/HF5 or whole-project completion.

Media links are obtained only from original helper/display seal path metadata; the template does not open, decode, hash or regenerate media. It reads no NPZ/scientific archive and imports no HF/NumPy/PIL. Only ordinary JSON/MD, old raw front bytes and their hashes are accessed by its future execution.

All six current front files are preflighted byte-exact to git show BASE before formal documentation is written. Their new prefixes are concatenated with the original raw bytes and checked as a unique unchanged suffix. front_history records original byte lengths/SHA for the publisher to verify.

RESULTS/NEXT_STEPS/closure/front_history outputs require fresh paths. Old scientific sources, original25 tasks/results, protocol, seals and stored arrays are not rewritten. Scope and qualification limits are explicit in RESULTS, closure and every front prefix.

The default next-step text branches on real execution outcome: successful transport suggests minimal external consumption/necessary finite reference planning; display-only failure reuses already saved results under a new explicit scope; other failure preserves first-error evidence without automatic retries, relaxation or clock extension. No next step is executed by this template.

Publication/remote recovery is deferred to its actual separate receipt. The closure does not assert the new records are already committed/pushed/restored. Actual review and pixel-QA statuses are displayed independently; no image inspection or independent review is fabricated.
acceptable_scope_limits: This review asserts source readiness only, not an actual terminal outcome, cache gate pass, graph quality or closed record PASS.

The template expects ordinary final files in the already-frozen schema. Malformed JSON or inconsistent ordinary data is allowed to raise; no repair, recomputation or generic recovery framework is added.
Optional --next-plan is a later ordinary Markdown choice from actual outcomes, not authorization for its proposed execution.
The status of the overall scientific/card execution and the status of later publication are distinct. Independent actual-review requirements remain enforced by the separately reviewed publisher.
